title: Repairing BT818 in place, triaging the prose sweep, q=9 by MILP, and the Hoffman-tight coclique as a regular simplex carrying D4 triality
purpose: Eight fronts. (1) Correct BT818's prose in place -- its alpha_exact=7 field is right, only the `correction` string and docstring say 9 -- without touching the correct computation. (2) Triage the remaining 441 prose/data findings beyond the hand-checked ten, and report a precision measured on a larger sample. (3) alpha(W(3,9)) by symmetry-broken MILP at 820 vertices, the only thing that turns the deficit sequence 3,8 into three points. (4) Apply the Pass5278 frame identity to the other lane's NO_5^+(5): Hoffman 13 predicts noncollinear inner product -1/12, making their 13-coclique a regular 12-simplex. (5) Test whether the order-576 W(D4):C3 stabiliser they proved at Pass5308 acts on that simplex, since a simplex in R^12 is where triality could live. Bonkers: (6) sweep DOCSTRINGS against certificates, since BT818's worst error was in its docstring and the guard only reads JSON prose fields; (7) ask whether alpha=9 was ever true of a DIFFERENT graph, which would make BT818 a coordinate artefact rather than a typo; (8) two-distance bounds using BOTH inner products, the one thing Hoffman structurally cannot see.
boundary: alpha(W(3,3))=7 is Pass4795/Pass4800's and is cited, not reclaimed. Front (3) yields a bound only if the MILP proves optimality; a timeout is a lower bound and must be labelled one, and at 820 vertices timing out is the likely outcome. Front (5) tests an ACTION, not an isomorphism -- exhibiting a group acting on a simplex does not identify it with the simplex's full symmetry group S_13. Front (8) is an open direction: no two-distance bound improving on Hoffman is claimed to exist, and failing to construct one establishes nothing. Front (2)'s precision figure will remain a sample estimate, not a corpus census.
prior_art_check: Searched for the RESULT before reserving: the frame/Hoffman identification is Pass5278-5279 (this lane); the two-distance tight frame is the other lane's Pass5261; W(D4):C3 order 576 is their Pass5308; the 13-coclique is their Pass5212. The simplex reading of a Hoffman-TIGHT coclique was searched for under 'regular simplex', 'equiangular', 'constant inner product' and found only in unrelated senses -- their Pass5291 simplex is the binary [15,4,8] code, and w33_frame_hoffman_resolution_theorem uses 'frame' for a pair of disjoint lines.
